requirements.evidence: Contract met: CallMode enum with the three string cases (app/Enums/CallMode.php:7-9), NoWaitingTicketsException extends RuntimeException (app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php:7), invokable CallNextTicket with the exact signature (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:31). Queue row locked and is_active read from DB inside the transaction (:37-44); waiting + queue filter and priority desc/issued_at/id ordering (:79-85); modes (:87-91); fairness reads last 3 called by called_at desc, id desc and requires a waiting normal (:100-119); candidate row lock + status re-check with skip-and-reselect loop (:48-66); only status/called_at/called_by_user_id set and the model returned (:55-61). Both docs updated. Edge: history filters status = Called (:104), which would drop tickets that later move to another status, but no such transition exists in this task's scope.

conventions.evidence: Domain write is an Action in app/Actions with PHPDoc on the public method (:16-30); no service/repository layer; docs/business-rules.md and docs/architecture.md updated including the TODO about linking the concurrency test; CHANGELOG entry under Added (CHANGELOG.md:21); Pest feature test shipped.

security.evidence: Authorization explicitly out of scope per task and documented as the caller's responsibility (docs/business-rules.md:'Authorization: who may call is not checked by this action'). No mass assignment: fields set individually (CallNextTicket.php:56-58); queue state taken from a locked DB read rather than the passed instance (:37-44); no user input or output rendering.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php covers returned model state and persistence (:31-47), ordering and tie-break by id (:49-72), queue isolation (:82-89), already-called exclusion (:91-102), fairness trigger, no-normal fallback and streak reset with time travel (:104-166), priority_only counting toward streak (:168-182), each mode (:184-213), NoWaitingTickets dataset with no-change assertions (:215-230), inactive queue using a stale model instance (:232-243), and a simulated concurrent call via DB::beforeExecuting (:245-274). Small gap: no test that a normal_only call resets the streak.

simplicity.evidence: Lean: one action with two small private helpers, plain query builder. Minor: fairnessRequiresNormal() is re-evaluated on every loop iteration (CallNextTicket.php:87) and the winner is marked by hand rather than reusing Ticket::call(), though the hand-rolled write is justified by the lock/re-check requirement.

readability.evidence: Clear names (nextCandidate, fairnessRequiresNormal, FAIRNESS_STREAK constant at :20), short focused methods, comments explain why (:35-37, :65), no dead code or debug output; tests read as specifications with descriptive it() names.

scope.evidence: Diff limited to the action, enum, exception, its test, the two required docs and a CHANGELOG line; no HTTP/Livewire/authorization code added.

issues.explanation: The fairness history filters on status = Called, so once tickets move to a later status (served/recall/skip in future work) they would vanish from the last-3-calls window; filtering on whereNotNull('called_at') would be more robust.
Only priority_only calls are tested as counting toward the streak; there is no test that a normal_only call resets it, although the task states calls in both restricted modes count in the history.
fairnessRequiresNormal() runs two extra queries on every skip-and-reselect iteration; it could be computed once per call, re-checked only if needed.
The race simulation keys on SQL text matching ('from "tickets"' and '"id" = ?'), which is brittle against query-builder changes; acceptable but worth a comment that it is SQLite/grammar specific.

review.summary: Implements CallNextTicket with the CallMode enum, NoWaitingTicketsException, queue-row and candidate-row locking with skip-and-reselect, the 3-call fairness rule, and docs/CHANGELOG updates, backed by a thorough Pest suite including a simulated concurrent call. The code is lean, readable and on-scope; only minor points remain (status-based fairness history, a missing normal_only streak-reset test), so it is approvable with nits.
